Stability of Superposition of Viscous Contact Wave and Rarefaction Waves for Compressible Navier-Stokes System

Feimin Huang ††thanks: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, P. R. China and Beijing Center of Mathematics and Information Sciences, Beijing 100048, P. R. China (fhuang@amt.ac.cn). The work of F. Huang is partially supported by the NSFC Grants No. 11371349, National Basic Research Program of China (973 Program) under Grant No. 2011CB808002.    Teng Wang ††thanks: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, P. R. China (tengwang@amss.ac.cn).
Abstract

This paper is concerned with the large-time behavior of solutions for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system. We show that the combination of viscous contact wave with rarefaction waves for the non-isentropic polytropic gas is stable under large initial perturbation without the condition that the adiabatic exponent γ\gamma is close to 1, provided the strength of the combination waves is suitably small.

Key words and phrases: viscous contact discontinuity, compressible Navier-Stokes system, stability, large initial perturbation

1 Introduction

The one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system in Lagrangian coordinates read

{vt−ux=0,ut+px=μ​(uxv)x,(e+u22)t+(p​u)x=(κ​θxv+μ​u​uxv)x\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle v_{t}-u_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle u_{t}+p_{x}=\mu\left(\frac{u_{x}}{v}\right)_{x},\\ \displaystyle\left(e+\frac{u^{2}}{2}\right)_{t}+\left(pu\right)_{x}=\left(\kappa\frac{\theta_{x}}{v}+\mu\frac{uu_{x}}{v}\right)_{x}\end{array}\right. (1.1)

for x∈ℝ=(−∞,+∞)x\in\mathbb{R}=(-\infty,+\infty), t>0t>0, where v⁡(x,t)>0v(x,t)>0, u⁡(x,t)u(x,t), θ⁡(x,t)>0\theta(x,t)>0, e⁡(x,t)>0e(x,t)>0 and p⁡(x,t)p(x,t) are the specific volume, fluid velocity, absolute temperature, internal energy and pressure, respectively, while the positive constants μ\mu and κ\kappa denote the viscosity and heat conduction coefficients, respectively. Here we study the ideal polytropic fluids so that pp and ee are given by the state equations

p=R​θv=A​v−γ​exp⁡(γ−1R​s),e=cν​θ+const.,\displaystyle p=\frac{R\theta}{v}=Av^{-\gamma}\exp\left(\frac{\gamma-1}{R}s\right),\hskip 10.00002pte=c_{\nu}\theta+\mathrm{const}.,

where ss is the entropy, γ>1\gamma>1 is the adiabatic exponent, cν=Rγ−1c_{\nu}=\frac{R}{\gamma-1} is the specific heat, and AA and RR are both positive constants. We consider the Cauchy problem to the system (1.1) supplement with the following initial and far field conditions:

{(v,u,θ)​(x,0)=(v0,u0,θ0)​(x),x∈ℝ,(v,u,θ)​(±∞,t)=(v±,u±,θ±),t>0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle(v,u,\theta)(x,0)=(v_{0},u_{0},\theta_{0})(x),&\displaystyle x\in\mathbb{R},\\ \displaystyle(v,u,\theta)(\pm\infty,t)=(v_{\pm},u_{\pm},\theta_{\pm}),&\displaystyle t>0,\end{array}\right. (1.2)

where v±(>0)v_{\pm}(>0), u±u_{\pm} and θ±(>0)\theta_{\pm}(>0) are given constants, and we assume infℝv0>0\inf_{\mathbb{R}}v_{0}>0, infℝθ0>0\inf_{\mathbb{R}}\theta_{0}>0, and (v0,u0,θ0)​(±∞)=(v±,u±,θ±)(v_{0},u_{0},\theta_{0})(\pm\infty)=(v_{\pm},u_{\pm},\theta_{\pm}) as compatibility conditions. When the far field states are the same, i.e., v+=v−v_{+}=v_{-}, u+=u−u_{+}=u_{-}, θ+=θ−\theta_{+}=\theta_{-}, there has been considerable progress on the global existence of the solutions to the system (1.1) since 1977, see [11, 12, 14, 15, 17] and the reference therein. In particular, Jiang [11, 12] first obtained some interesting results on the large-time behavior of solutions, however the temperature is only shown to be locally bounded in space. More recently, Li and Liang [17] improved Jiang’s results by proving the temperature is uniformly bounded.

The existence and large time behavior of solutions to the system (1.1) with different end states become much more complicated. It is noted that, if the dissipation effects are neglected, i.e., μ=κ=0\mu=\kappa=0, the system (1.1) is reduced to the compressible Euler equations as follows

{vt−ux=0,ut+px=0,(e+u22)t+(p​u)x=0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle v_{t}-u_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle u_{t}+p_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle\left(e+\frac{u^{2}}{2}\right)_{t}+\left(pu\right)_{x}=0,\end{array}\right. (1.3)

which is the most important hyperbolic system of conservation laws. It is well known that the system (1.3) has rich wave phenomena. Indeed, it contains three basic wave patterns (see [24]), two nonlinear waves: shock and rarefaction wave, and a linearly degenerate wave: contact discontinuity. When we consider the Riemann initial data

(v,u,θ)​(x,0)={(v−,u−,θ−),x<0,(v+,u+,θ+),x>0,(v,u,\theta)(x,0)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}),&\displaystyle x<0,\\ \displaystyle(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+}),&\displaystyle x>0,\end{array}\right. (1.4)

the solutions consist of the above three wave patterns and their superpositions, called by Riemann solutions, and govern both the local and large time asymptotic behavior of general solutions of the system (1.3). It is of great importance and interest to study the large-time behavior of the viscous version of these basic wave patterns and their superpositions to the compressible Navier-Stokes system (1.1).

There has been extensive literature on the stability analysis of viscous wave pattern to system (1.1), meanwhile new phenomena has been discovered and new techniques have been developed. We refer to [5, 13, 20] for the shock wave, [21, 22, 23] for the rarefaction wave, [6, 7, 8, 9, 10] for the viscous contact discontinuity, and the reference therein. However, the stability of the superposition of several wave patterns is more complicated and challenging due to the fact that the stability analysis essentially depends on the underlying properties of basic wave pattern and these frameworks are not compatible with each other. Besides, the wave interaction between different families of wave patterns is complicated. Recently, Huang-Matsumura in [5] showed that the superposition of the two viscous shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes system (1.1) is asymptotically stable without the zero initial mass condition. This result was extended in [4] to the combination of viscous contact discontinuity with rarefaction waves by deriving new estimates on the heat kernel. The time-asymptotic stability of other cases is still open!

It is noted that all results mentioned above are concerned with the small perturbation around the viscous wave pattern. In another word, they are “local” stability. A nature problem is, whether or not these basic wave patterns and their linear superpositions are stable even for large perturbation. This is equivalent to study the global stability of the viscous wave patterns to the system (1.1), which is challenging because the nonlinear terms play leading role in the large solutions, while the linearized system around wave patterns is essential for the local stability. Along this direction, Nishihara-Yang-Zhao in [23] first proved the rarefaction waves for the system (1.1) are stable with “partially” large perturbation with the condition that the adiabatic exponent γ\gamma is closing enough to “1”. Precisely speaking, the amplitude of initial perturbation is reciprocal to γ−1\gamma-1. That is, γ−1\gamma-1 is smaller, the perturbation around the rarefaction wave can be larger. This result is extended by Huang-Zhao in [10] to the case of single viscous contact wave and the combination of viscous contact wave and rarefaction waves for a free boundary value problem, and further by Hong in [3] for the Cauchy problem. Note that the condition on γ\gamma plays essential role in [3, 10, 23], however, it is not natural in the physical setting. The main aim of this paper is to remove the non-physical condition of the adiabatic exponent γ\gamma.

Before stating the main results, we first recall the viscous contact wave (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) for the compressible Navier-Stokes system (1.1) introduced in [8]. For the Riemann problem (1.3)-(1.4), it is known that the contact discontinuity solution takes the form

(V~,U~,Θ~)​(x,t)={(v−,u−,θ−),x​<0,t>​0,(v+,u+,θ+),x>0,t>0,(\tilde{V},\tilde{U},\tilde{\Theta})(x,t)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}),&\displaystyle x<0,t>0,\\ \displaystyle(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+}),&\displaystyle x>0,t>0,\end{array}\right. (1.5)

provide that

u−=u+,p−≜R​θ−v−=p+≜R​θ+v+.\displaystyle u_{-}=u_{+},\hskip 10.00002ptp_{-}\triangleq\frac{R\theta_{-}}{v_{-}}=p_{+}\triangleq\frac{R\theta_{+}}{v_{+}}. (1.6)

We assume that u−=u+=0u_{-}=u_{+}=0 without loss of generality. Due to the effect of heat conductivity, the contact discontinuity (V~,U~,Θ~)(\tilde{V},\tilde{U},\tilde{\Theta}) is smoothed and behaves as a diffusion wave, called by ”viscous contact wave”. The viscous contact wave (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) can be constructed as follows. Since the pressure for the profile (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) is expected to be constant asymptotically, we set

Θt=a​(ΘxΘ)x,Θ⁡(±∞,t)=θ±,a=κ​p+​(γ−1)γ​R2>0,\displaystyle\Theta_{t}=a\left(\frac{\Theta_{x}}{\Theta}\right)_{x},\hskip 10.00002pt\Theta(\pm\infty,t)=\theta_{\pm},\hskip 10.00002pta=\frac{\kappa p_{+}(\gamma-1)}{\gamma R^{2}}>0, (1.8)

(1+t)|Θx​x|+(1+t)12​|Θx|+|Θ−θ±|=O⁡(1)​δ​e−c1​x21+tas|x|→∞,\displaystyle(1+t)|\Theta_{xx}|+(1+t)^{\frac{1}{2}}|\Theta_{x}|+|\Theta-\theta_{\pm}|=O(1)\delta e^{-\frac{c_{1}x^{2}}{1+t}}\hskip 10.00002pt\mathrm{as}~|x|\rightarrow\infty, (1.9)

where c1c_{1} is positive constant depending only on θ±\theta_{\pm}. Once Θ\Theta is determined, the contact wave profile (V,U,Θ)​(x,t)(V,U,\Theta)(x,t) is then defined as follows:

V=Rp+​Θ,U=κ⁡(γ−1)γ​R​ΘxΘ,Θ=Θ.\displaystyle V=\frac{R}{p_{+}}\Theta,\hskip 10.00002ptU=\frac{\kappa(\gamma-1)}{\gamma R}\frac{\Theta_{x}}{\Theta},\hskip 10.00002pt\Theta=\Theta. (1.10)

The contact wave (V,U,Θ)​(x,t)(V,U,\Theta)(x,t) solves the compressible Navier-Stokes system (1.1) time asymptotically, that is,

{Vt−Ux=0,Ut+(R​ΘV)x=μ​(UxV)x+R1,cν​Θt+p⁡(V,Θ)​Ux=(κ​ΘxV)x+μ​Ux2V+R2,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle V_{t}-U_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle U_{t}+\left(\frac{R\Theta}{V}\right)_{x}=\mu\left(\frac{U_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}+R_{1},\\ \displaystyle c_{\nu}\Theta_{t}+p(V,\Theta)U_{x}=\left(\kappa\frac{\Theta_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}+\mu\frac{U^{2}_{x}}{V}+R_{2},\end{array}\right. (1.11)

where

We first study the global stability of single viscous contact wave (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) for arbitrary γ>1\gamma>1. For this, we put the perturbation (ϕ,ψ,ζ)​(x,t)(\phi,\psi,\zeta)(x,t) by

(ϕ,ψ,ζ)​(x,t)=(v−V,u−U,θ−Θ)​(x,t).(\phi,\psi,\zeta)(x,t)=(v-V,u-U,\theta-\Theta)(x,t). (1.13)

The precise statement of the first result is

Theorem 1.1

(Viscous contact wave) For any given left end state (v−,u−,θ−)(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}), suppose that the right end state (v+,u+,θ+)(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+}) satisfies (1.6). Let (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) be the viscous contact wave defined in (1.10) with strength δ=|θ+−θ−|\delta=|\theta_{+}-\theta_{-}|. There exist a function m⁡(δ)m(\delta) satisfying m⁡(δ)→+∞m(\delta)\to+\infty, as δ→0\delta\to 0 and a small constant δ0\delta_{0} such that if δ<δ0\delta<\delta_{0} and the initial data satisfies

{v0​(x),θ0​(x)≥m0−1,m0=:m⁡(δ0),‖(v0​(x)−V⁡(x,0),u0​(x)−U⁡(x,0),θ0​(x)−Θ⁡(x,0))‖H1​(ℝ)≤m0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle v_{0}(x),\theta_{0}(x)\geq m_{0}^{-1},\quad m_{0}=:m(\delta_{0}),\\[5.69046pt] \|(v_{0}(x)-V(x,0),u_{0}(x)-U(x,0),\theta_{0}(x)-\Theta(x,0))\|_{H^{1}(\mathbb{R})}\leq m_{0},\end{array}\right. (1.14)

then the Cauchy problem (1.1)-(1.2) admits a unique global solution (v,u,θ)(v,u,\theta) satisfying

(v−V,u−U,θ−Θ)​(x,t)∈C⁡((0,+∞),H1​(ℝ));(v-V,u-U,\theta-\Theta)(x,t)\in C\big((0,+\infty);H^{1}(\mathbb{R})\big);
(v−V)x​(x,t)∈L2​(0,+∞,L2​(ℝ));(v-V)_{x}(x,t)\in L^{2}(0,+\infty;L^{2}\big(\mathbb{R})\big);
(u−U,θ−Θ)x​(x,t)∈L2​(0,+∞,H1​(ℝ)).(u-U,\theta-\Theta)_{x}(x,t)\in L^{2}\big(0,+\infty;H^{1}(\mathbb{R})\big).

Furthermore,

limt→+∞supx∈ℝ|(v−V,u−U,θ−Θ)​(x,t)|=0.\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left|(v-V,u-U,\theta-\Theta)(x,t)\right|=0. (1.15)
Remark 1

Theorem 1.1 means that if the strength of contact wave is smaller, the initial perturbation can be larger. In particular, when δ=0\delta=0, that is, the asymptotic state is a constant one (v¯,u¯,θ¯)(\bar{v},\bar{u},\bar{\theta}) instead of a wave pattern, then for any initial data (v0−v¯,u0−u¯,θ0−θ¯)​(x)∈H1​(ℝ)(v_{0}-\bar{v},u_{0}-\bar{u},\theta_{0}-\bar{\theta})(x)\in H^{1}(\mathbb{R}), there always exists a small constant δ0\delta_{0} such that (1.14) holds, in which the second term is replaced by ‖(v0​(x)−v¯,u0​(x)−u¯,θ0​(x)−θ¯)‖H1​(ℝ)≤m0\|(v_{0}(x)-\bar{v},u_{0}(x)-\bar{u},\theta_{0}(x)-\bar{\theta})\|_{H^{1}(\mathbb{R})}\leq m_{0}. This coincides with the one in Li-Liang [17].

Remark 2

Theorem 1.1 holds for any γ>1\gamma>1 and thus removes the condition that γ\gamma is close to 1 in Nishihara-Yang-Zhao [23] and also in [3, 10].

When the relation (1.6) fails, the basic theory of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws implies that for any given constant state (v−,u−,θ−)(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}) with v−>0v_{-}>0, θ−>0\theta_{-}>0 and u−∈ℝu_{-}\in\mathbb{R}, there exists a suitable neighborhood Ω⁡(v−,u−,θ−)\Omega(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}) of (v−,u−,θ−)(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}) such that for any (v+,u+,θ+)∈Ω⁡(v−,u−,θ−)(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+})\in\Omega(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}), the Riemann problem of the Euler system (1.3), (1.4) has a unique solution. In this paper, we only consider the case of the superposition of the viscous contact wave and rarefaction waves with

where

and

s=Rγ−1​ln​R​θA+R​ln​v,s±=Rγ−1​ln​R​θ±A+R​ln​v±,λ±​(v,s)=±A​γ​v−γ−1​eγ−1R​s.s=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}\ln\frac{R\theta}{A}+R\ln v,\hskip 10.00002pts_{\pm}=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}\ln\frac{R\theta_{\pm}}{A}+R\ln v_{\pm},~~\lambda_{\pm}(v,s)=\pm\sqrt{A\gamma v^{-\gamma-1}e^{\frac{\gamma-1}{R}s}}.

the points (v−m,um,θ−m)(v_{-}^{m},u^{m},\theta_{-}^{m}) and (v+m,um,θ+m)(v_{+}^{m},u^{m},\theta_{+}^{m}) belong to the 1-rarefaction wave curve R−​(v−,u−,θ−)R_{-}(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}) and the 3-rarefaction wave curve R+​(v+,u+,θ+)R_{+}(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+}), respectively, where

R±(v±,u±,θ±)={(v,u,θ)|s=s±,u=u±−∫v±vλ±(η,s±)dη,v>v±}.R_{\pm}(v_{\pm},u_{\pm},\theta_{\pm})=\left\{(v,u,\theta)\Bigg|s=s_{\pm},u=u_{\pm}-\int_{v_{\pm}}^{v}\lambda_{\pm}(\eta,s_{\pm})d\eta,v>v_{\pm}\right\}.

Without loss of generality, we assume um=0u^{m}=0 in what follows. The 1-rarefaction wave (v−r,u−r,θ−r)​(xt)(v_{-}^{r},u_{-}^{r},\theta_{-}^{r})(\frac{x}{t}) (respectively the 3-rarefaction wave (v+r,u+r,θ+r)​(xt)(v_{+}^{r},u_{+}^{r},\theta_{+}^{r})(\frac{x}{t})) connecting (v−,u−,θ−)(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}) and (v−m,0,θ−m)(v_{-}^{m},0,\theta_{-}^{m}) (respectively (v+m,0,θ+m)(v_{+}^{m},0,\theta_{+}^{m}) and (v+,u+,θ+)(v_{+},u_{+},\theta_{+})) is the weak solution of the Riemann problem of the Euler system (1.3) with the following initial Riemann data

The precise statement of the second result is

Theorem 1.2

(Composite waves) For any given left end state (v−,u−,θ−)(v_{-},u_{-},\theta_{-}), let (V,U,Θ)(V,U,\Theta) be defined in (1.22) with strength satisfying (1.20). By (i​v)(iv) of Lemma 2.5, Theorem 1.2 implies

limt→+∞supx∈ℝ(|(v−v−r−Vc​d−v+r+v−m+v+m)​(x,t)||(u−Uc​d−u−r−u+r)​(x,t)||(θ−θ−r−Θc​d−θ+r+θ−m+θ+m)​(x,t)|)=0.\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\begin{array}[]{l}|(v-v_{-}^{r}-V^{cd}-v_{+}^{r}+v_{-}^{m}+v_{+}^{m})(x,t)|\\[5.69054pt] \quad\quad|(u-U^{cd}-u_{-}^{r}-u_{+}^{r})(x,t)|\\[5.69054pt] |(\theta-\theta_{-}^{r}-\Theta^{cd}-\theta_{+}^{r}+\theta_{-}^{m}+\theta_{+}^{m})(x,t)|\\[5.69054pt] \end{array}\right)=0.

We now explain the main strategy of this paper. It is noted that in [3, 10, 23], the smallness of γ−1\gamma-1 is used to control the lower and upper bound of the absolute temperature θ\theta. To remove the smallness condition of γ−1\gamma-1, the key point is to derive the uniform bound of θ\theta, which is also closely related to the uniform bound of the specific volume vv. Motivated by [11, 15, 17], we first obtain the basic energy estimate (see Lemma 3.1), which is independent of the time tt, with the help of the new estimates on the heat kernel developed in [4], provided the strengths of the waves are suitable small. It should be emphasized that the basic energy estimate is nontrivially obtained, while it is trivial for the case of small initial perturbation or the far-field condition being a constant one (v¯,u¯,θ¯)(\bar{v},\bar{u},\bar{\theta}). In fact, we essentially use the structure of wave patterns to control the terms involving the derivative of perturbation around the wave patterns. Secondly, the specific volume vv is shown uniformly bounded from below and above with respect to space and time through delicate analysis based on the basic energy estimate and a cut-off technique. Finally, we manipulate some weighted estimates on the perturbation around the wave patterns to derive the uniform bound of θ\theta. We remark that the underlying structures of viscous contact wave and rarefaction waves are essentially used throughout the whole proof, and the idea may not be valid for shock wave whose structure is quite different from those of viscous contact wave and rarefaction waves.

This paper is organized as follows. In the next section, we collect some useful lemmas and fundamental facts concerning the viscous contact wave as well as rarefaction waves. The main proof of Theorem 1.1 and 1.2 are completed in Section 3 and 4, respectively.

∥f∥Lp​(Ω):=(∫Ω|f(x)|pdx)1p,1≤p<∞,∥f∥L∞​(Ω):=ess.supΩ|f(x)|.\|f\|_{L^{p}(\Omega)}:=\left(\int_{\Omega}|f(x)|^{p}dx\right)^{\frac{1}{p}},\hskip 10.00002pt1\leq p<\infty,\hskip 10.00002pt\parallel f\parallel_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}:=\mbox{ess.sup}_{\Omega}|f(x)|.

Hk​(Ω)H^{k}(\Omega) denotes the kt​hk^{th} order Sobolev space with its norm

∥f∥Hk​(Ω):=(∑j=0k∥∂xjf∥2(Ω))12,when∥⋅∥=∥⋅∥L2​(Ω).\|f\|_{H^{k}(\Omega)}:=\left(\sum^{k}_{j=0}\parallel\partial^{j}_{x}f\parallel^{2}(\Omega)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}},\hskip 10.00002pt\mathrm{when}\parallel\cdot\parallel=\parallel\cdot\parallel_{L^{2}(\Omega)}.

The domain Ω\Omega will be often abbreviated without confusion.

3 Proof of Theorem 1.1

Substituting (1.11) into (1.1), (1.2) yields

{ϕt−ψx=0,ψt+(p−p+)x=μ​(uxv−UxV)x−R~1,cν​ζt+p​ux−p+​Ux=κ​(θxv−ΘxV)x+μ⁡(ux2v−Ux2V)−R~2,(ϕ,ψ,ζ)(x,0)=(ϕ0,ψ0,ζ0)(x),x∈ℝ.\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\phi_{t}-\psi_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle\psi_{t}+\left(p-p_{+}\right)_{x}=\mu\left(\frac{u_{x}}{v}-\frac{U_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}-\widetilde{R}_{1},\\ \displaystyle c_{\nu}\zeta_{t}+pu_{x}-p_{+}U_{x}=\kappa\left(\frac{\theta_{x}}{v}-\frac{\Theta_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}+\mu\left(\frac{u_{x}^{2}}{v}-\frac{U^{2}_{x}}{V}\right)-\widetilde{R}_{2},\\ \displaystyle(\phi,\psi,\zeta)(x,0)=(\phi_{0},\psi_{0},\zeta_{0})(x),\quad x\in\mathbb{R}.\end{array}\right. (3.1)

We shall prove Theorem 1.1 by the local existence and the a priori estimate. We look for the solution (ϕ,ψ,ζ)(\phi,\psi,\zeta) in the solution space X([0,+∞))X([0,+\infty)),

X([0,T])={(ϕ,ψ,ζ)|v,θ≥M−1,sup0≤t≤T∥(ϕ,ψ,ζ)∥H1≤M}\begin{array}[]{l}\displaystyle X([0,T])=\Big\{(\phi,\psi,\zeta)\Big|v,~\theta\geq M^{-1},\quad\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\|(\phi,\psi,\zeta)\|_{H^{1}}\leq M\Big\}\end{array}

for some 0<T≤+∞0<T\leq+\infty, where the constants MM will be determined later. Since the local existence of the solution is well known (for example, see [6]), to prove the global existence part of Theorem 1.1, we only need to establish the following a priori estimates.

Proposition 3.1

(A priori estimates) Assume that the conditions of Theorem 1.1 hold, then there exists a positive constant δ0\delta_{0} such that if δ<δ0\delta<\delta_{0} and (ϕ,ψ,ζ)∈X⁡([0,T])(\phi,\psi,\zeta)\in X([0,T]),

where C0C_{0} denotes a constant depending only on μ\mu, κ\kappa, RR, cνc_{\nu}, v±v_{\pm}, u±u_{\pm}, θ±\theta_{\pm} and m0m_{0}.

In Lemma 3.1, the smallness of δ\delta is used to guarantee that the basic energy (3.4) is only bounded by the initial data. |J1|=3R∫0t∫{ζ>Θ}ζ​ψ2​ψxvdxds+3R∫0t∫{ζ≤Θ}ζ​ψ2​ψxvdxds≤μ∫0t∫{ζ>Θ}ψ2​ψx2vdxds+C0∫0t∫{ζ>Θ}ζ2ψ2dxds+∫0t∫{ζ≤Θ}ψx2dxds+C0∫0t∫{ζ≤Θ}ζ2ψ4dxds≤μ​∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0tmaxx∈ℝ⁡(ζ−12​Θ)+2​(∫ψ2​𝑑x)​𝑑s+C∫0t∫{ζ≤Θ}ψx2θdxds+C0∫0tmaxx∈ℝψ4(∫{ζ≤Θ}ζ2dx)ds≤μ​∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2v​dx​ds+C0​∫0t(maxx∈ℝ⁡(ζ−12​Θ)+2+maxx∈ℝ⁡ψ4)​ds+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle|J_{1}|&\displaystyle=3R\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}\frac{\zeta\psi^{2}\psi_{x}}{v}dxds+3R\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\frac{\zeta\psi^{2}\psi_{x}}{v}dxds\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}\zeta^{2}\psi^{2}dxds\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle\quad+\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\psi_{x}^{2}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\zeta^{2}\psi^{4}dxds\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}\left(\int\psi^{2}dx\right)ds\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle\quad+C\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\left(\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\zeta^{2}dx\right)ds\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\left(\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}+\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\right)ds+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.66)

Recalling (3.4), (3.28), and using Cauchy’s inequality, it holds that

|J2|≤ε​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s+C⁡(ε−1,C0)​∫0t∫ϕ2​ψ4​𝑑x​𝑑s≤ε​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s+C⁡(ε−1,C0)​∫0tmaxx∈ℝ⁡ψ4​(∫ϕ2​𝑑x)​𝑑s≤ε​∫0t∫ψx2​dx​ds+C⁡(ε−1,C0)​∫0tmaxx∈ℝ⁡ψ4​ds.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle|J_{2}|&\displaystyle\leq\varepsilon\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds+C(\varepsilon^{-1},C_{0})\int_{0}^{t}\int\phi^{2}\psi^{4}dxds\\ &\displaystyle\leq\varepsilon\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds+C(\varepsilon^{-1},C_{0})\int_{0}^{t}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\left(\int\phi^{2}dx\right)ds\\ &\displaystyle\leq\varepsilon\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds+C(\varepsilon^{-1},C_{0})\int_{0}^{t}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}ds.\end{array} (3.67)

From (3.4), (2.3) and (3.17), one has

|J3|≤μ​∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ϕ2​ψ2​Ux2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ​∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C⁡(C0,M)​∫0t∫ϕ2​Ux2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ​∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2v​dx​ds+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle|J_{3}|&\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\phi^{2}\psi^{2}U_{x}^{2}dxds\\ &\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C(C_{0},M)\int_{0}^{t}\int\phi^{2}U_{x}^{2}dxds\\ &\displaystyle\leq\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.68)

By Lemma 2.1, (3.4), (2.3) and (3.17), we have

|J4|≤O⁡(1)​δ​∫0t∫(1+s)−1​|ψ|3​e−c1​x21+s​𝑑x​𝑑s≤C⁡(M)​δ​∫0t∫(1+s)−1​ψ2​e−c1​x21+s​dx​ds≤C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle|J_{4}|&\displaystyle\leq O(1)\delta\int_{0}^{t}\int(1+s)^{-1}|\psi|^{3}e^{-\frac{c_{1}x^{2}}{1+s}}dxds\\ &\displaystyle\leq C(M)\delta\int_{0}^{t}\int(1+s)^{-1}\psi^{2}e^{-\frac{c_{1}x^{2}}{1+s}}dxds\leq C_{0}.\end{array} (3.69)

Putting the estimates (3.66)-(3.69) into (3.65) gives

∫ψ4​𝑑x+∫0t∫ψ2​ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤C0+C0​ε​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s+C(ε−1,C0)∫0t(maxx∈ℝ(ζ−12Θ)+2+maxx∈ℝψ4)ds.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\int\psi^{4}dx+\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\varepsilon\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\qquad+C(\varepsilon^{-1},C_{0})\int_{0}^{t}\left(\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}+\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\right)ds.\end{array} (3.70)

Noticing that

2​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤∫0t∫ψx2θ​𝑑x​𝑑s+∫0t∫θ​ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤C0+C0​∫0t∫θ​ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s.\displaystyle 2\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\leq\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dxds+\int_{0}^{t}\int\theta\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\theta\psi_{x}^{2}dxds. (3.71)

Combining (3.64) and (3.70), choosing ε\varepsilon suitable small, we have

∫((ζ−Θ)+2+ψ4)​𝑑x+∫0t∫((ψ2+θ)​ψx2+ζx2)​𝑑x​𝑑s≤C0+C0​∫0t(maxx∈ℝ⁡(ζ−12​Θ)+2+maxx∈ℝ⁡ψ4)​ds.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\int((\zeta-\Theta)_{+}^{2}+\psi^{4})dx+\int_{0}^{t}\int((\psi^{2}+\theta)\psi_{x}^{2}+\zeta_{x}^{2})dxds\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\left(\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}+\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\right)ds.\end{array} (3.72)

Step 3.  It remains to estimate the last two terms on the right hand side of (3.72). For x∈ℝx\in\mathbb{R},

(ζ−12​Θ)+2=∫−∞x2​(ζ−12​Θ)+​(ζx−12​Θx)​𝑑x≤C​∫(ζ−12​Θ)+​(|ζx|+|Θx|)​𝑑x≤ε∫(ζ−12Θ)+2θdx+Cε∫{ζ>Θ2}(ζx2θ+Θx2θ)dx≤3ε∫(ζ−12Θ)+2ζdx+Cε∫ζx2θdx+Cε∫{ζ>Θ2}ζ2Θx2dx≤3εmaxx∈ℝ(ζ−12Θ)+2∫{ζ>Θ2}ζdx+Cε∫ζx2θdx+Cε∫ζ2Θx2dx≤ε​C0​maxx∈ℝ​(ζ−12​Θ)+2+Cε​∫ζx2θ​dx+Cε​∫ζ2​Θx2​dx.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}=\int_{-\infty}^{x}2\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}\left(\zeta_{x}-\frac{1}{2}\Theta_{x}\right)dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq C\int\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}(|\zeta_{x}|+|\Theta_{x}|)dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\varepsilon\int\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}\theta dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int_{\{\zeta>\frac{\Theta}{2}\}}\left(\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}+\frac{\Theta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}\right)dx\\[11.38109pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq 3\varepsilon\int\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}\zeta dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int_{\{\zeta>\frac{\Theta}{2}\}}\zeta^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq 3\varepsilon\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}\int_{\{\zeta>\frac{\Theta}{2}\}}\zeta dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\zeta^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\varepsilon C_{0}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left(\zeta-\frac{1}{2}\Theta\right)_{+}^{2}+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\zeta^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}dx.\end{array} (3.73)

This yields

ψ4=∫−∞x4ψ3ψxdx≤4∫{ζ>Θ}|ψ|3|ψx|dx+4∫{ζ≤Θ}|ψ|3|ψx|dx≤ε∫{ζ>Θ}|ψ|5θdx+Cε∫{ζ>Θ}ψx2|ψ|θdx+ε∫{ζ≤Θ}ψ6θdx+Cε∫{ζ≤Θ}ψx2θdx≤εmaxx∈ℝψ4∫{ζ>Θ}(ψ2+θ)dx+Cεmaxx∈ℝψ4∫{ζ≤Θ}ψ2dx+Cε∫ψx2(|ψ|θ+1θ)dx≤ε​C0​maxx∈ℝ​ψ4+Cε​∫ψx2​(|ψ|θ+1θ)​dx,\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\psi^{4}=\int_{-\infty}^{x}4\psi^{3}\psi_{x}dx\leq 4\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}|\psi|^{3}|\psi_{x}|dx+4\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}|\psi|^{3}|\psi_{x}|dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\varepsilon\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}|\psi|^{5}\sqrt{\theta}dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}\psi_{x}^{2}\frac{|\psi|}{\sqrt{\theta}}dx+\varepsilon\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\psi^{6}\theta dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta}dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\varepsilon\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\int_{\{\zeta>\Theta\}}(\psi^{2}+\theta)dx+C\varepsilon\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}\int_{\{\zeta\leq\Theta\}}\psi^{2}dx+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\psi_{x}^{2}\left(\frac{|\psi|}{\sqrt{\theta}}+\frac{1}{\theta}\right)dx\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\varepsilon C_{0}\max_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\psi^{4}+\frac{C}{\varepsilon}\int\psi_{x}^{2}\left(\frac{|\psi|}{\sqrt{\theta}}+\frac{1}{\theta}\right)dx,\end{array} (3.75)

which directly gives

Substituting (3.74) and (3.76) into (3.72), recalling (3.4), (2.3) and (3.17), and choosing ε\varepsilon suitable small, it holds that

sup0≤t≤T∫((ζ−Θ)+2+ψ4)​𝑑x+∫0T∫((ψ2+θ)​ψx2+ζx2)​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0+C0​∫0T∫(ζx2θ+ψx2​(|ψ|θ+1θ))​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0+12​∫0T∫(ζx2+ψ2​ψx2)​𝑑x​𝑑t+C0​∫0T∫(ζx2θ2+ψx2θ)​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0+12​∫0T∫(ζx2+ψ2​ψx2)​dx​dt.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\int((\zeta-\Theta)_{+}^{2}+\psi^{4})dx+\int_{0}^{T}\int((\psi^{2}+\theta)\psi_{x}^{2}+\zeta_{x}^{2})dxdt\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\int_{0}^{T}\int\left(\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}+\psi_{x}^{2}\left(\frac{|\psi|}{\sqrt{\theta}}+\frac{1}{\theta}\right)\right)dxdt\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq C_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{T}\int(\zeta_{x}^{2}+\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2})dxdt+C_{0}\int_{0}^{T}\int\left(\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta^{2}}+\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta}\right)dxdt\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq C_{0}+\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{T}\int(\zeta_{x}^{2}+\psi^{2}\psi_{x}^{2})dxdt.\end{array} (3.77)

From(3.4), (3.46), we have

∫{ζ≤2Θ}ζ2dx≤C∫ℝΦ(θΘ)dx≤C0,\displaystyle\int_{\{\zeta\leq 2\Theta\}}\zeta^{2}dx\leq C\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi\left(\frac{\theta}{\Theta}\right)dx\leq C_{0}, (3.78)

and

Thus combining (3.77)-(3.79), the proof of Lemma 3.5 is completed. □\Box

Lemma 3.6

Suppose that (ϕ,ψ,ζ)∈X⁡([0,T])(\phi,\psi,\zeta)\in X([0,T]) satisfies δ=|θ+−θ−|≤δ0\delta=|\theta_{+}-\theta_{-}|\leq\delta_{0} with suitable small δ0\delta_{0}, it holds

sup0≤t≤T∫(ϕx2+ψx2+ζx2)​𝑑x+∫0T∫(θ​ϕx2+ψx​x2+ζx​x2)​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0.\displaystyle\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\int(\phi_{x}^{2}+\psi_{x}^{2}+\zeta_{x}^{2})dx+\int_{0}^{T}\int(\theta\phi_{x}^{2}+\psi_{xx}^{2}+\zeta_{xx}^{2})dxdt\leq C_{0}. (3.80)

Proof: Due to (3.4), (3.28) and (3.45), some terms of (3.13) can be considered more carefully, that is,

|Rv​ζx​v~xv~|+|ψx​Ux​(1v−1V)|+ψx2v≤R​θ4​v​(v~xv~)2+C0​ζx2θ+C0​ψx2+C0​ϕ2​Ux2≤R​θ4​v​(v~xv~)2+C0​(ζx2+ζx2θ2+θ​ψx2+ψx2θ)+C0​ϕ2​Ux2.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\left|\frac{R}{v}\zeta_{x}\frac{\tilde{v}_{x}}{\tilde{v}}\right|+\left|\psi_{x}U_{x}\left(\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{V}\right)\right|+\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{v}\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\leq\frac{R\theta}{4v}\left(\frac{\tilde{v}_{x}}{\tilde{v}}\right)^{2}+C_{0}\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta}+C_{0}\psi_{x}^{2}+C_{0}\phi^{2}U_{x}^{2}\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\leq\frac{R\theta}{4v}\left(\frac{\tilde{v}_{x}}{\tilde{v}}\right)^{2}+C_{0}\left(\zeta_{x}^{2}+\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta^{2}}+\theta\psi_{x}^{2}+\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta}\right)+C_{0}\phi^{2}U_{x}^{2}.\end{array} (3.81)

The other terms in (3.13) can be estimated the same as in step 2 in Lemma 3.1. Integrating (3.13) over ℝ×(0,t)\mathbb{R}\times(0,t), recalling (3.4) and (3.45), we have

sup0≤t≤T∫ϕx2​𝑑x+∫0T∫θ​ϕx2​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0.\displaystyle\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\int\phi_{x}^{2}dx+\int_{0}^{T}\int\theta\phi_{x}^{2}dxdt\leq C_{0}. (3.82)

Multiplying (3.1)2\eqref{perturb}_{2} by −ψx​x-\psi_{xx}, integrating the resulted equation over ℝ×(0,t)\mathbb{R}\times(0,t), and noticing that

(p−p+)x=(R​ζ−p+​ϕv)x=R​ζx−p+​ϕxv−R​ζ−p+​ϕv2​ϕx−R​ζ−p+​ϕv2​Vx=R​ζxv−R​θ​ϕxv2−R​ζ−p+​ϕv2​Vx.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle(p-p_{+})_{x}&\displaystyle=\left(\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v}\right)_{x}=\frac{R\zeta_{x}-p_{+}\phi_{x}}{v}-\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v^{2}}\phi_{x}-\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v^{2}}V_{x}\\[8.53581pt] &\displaystyle=\frac{R\zeta_{x}}{v}-\frac{R\theta\phi_{x}}{v^{2}}-\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v^{2}}V_{x}.\end{array}

Then we have

∫ψx22​𝑑x+μ​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s=∫ψ0​x22​𝑑x+∫0t∫(R​ζxv−R​θ​ϕxv2−R​ζ−p+​ϕv2​Vx)​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s−μ∫0t∫ψx(1v)xψx​xdxds+μ∫0t∫(UxV−Uxv)xψx​xdxds+∫0t∫R~1ψx​xdxds.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\int\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{2}dx+\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds=\int\frac{\psi_{0x}^{2}}{2}dx+\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{R\zeta_{x}}{v}-\frac{R\theta\phi_{x}}{v^{2}}-\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v^{2}}V_{x}\right)\psi_{xx}dxds\\ \displaystyle\quad-\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)_{x}\psi_{xx}dxds+\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{U_{x}}{V}-\frac{U_{x}}{v}\right)_{x}\psi_{xx}dxds+\int_{0}^{t}\int\widetilde{R}_{1}\psi_{xx}dxds.\end{array} (3.83)

In the following, each term on the right hand side of (3.83) will be estimated. From (2.3), (3.45) and (3.82), one has

|∫0t∫(R​ζxv−R​θ​ϕxv2−R​ζ−p+​ϕv2​Vx)​ψx​x​dx​ds|≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ζx2+θ2​ϕx2+(ϕ2+ζ2)​Θx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0+maxx,t⁡θ​∫0t∫θ​ϕx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​dx​ds+C0+C0​maxx,t​θ.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\left|\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{R\zeta_{x}}{v}-\frac{R\theta\phi_{x}}{v^{2}}-\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v^{2}}V_{x}\right)\psi_{xx}dxds\right|\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\zeta_{x}^{2}+\theta^{2}\phi_{x}^{2}+(\phi^{2}+\zeta^{2})\Theta_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}+\max_{x,t}\theta\int_{0}^{t}\int\theta\phi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta.\end{array} (3.84)

By Cauchy’s inequality and Sobolev’s inequality, and recalling (3.4), (3.45), (3.71) and (3.82), we obtain

|μ​∫0t∫ψx​(1v)x​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s|≤C​∫0t∫|ψx​ϕx​ψx​xv2|+|ψx​Vx​ψx​xv2|​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ψx2​ϕx2+ψx2​Θx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t‖ψx‖L∞2​‖ϕx‖2​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t‖ψx‖|ψx​x|𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ4​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ4​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​dx​ds+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\left|\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)_{x}\psi_{xx}dxds\right|\leq C\int_{0}^{t}\int\left|\frac{\psi_{x}\phi_{x}\psi_{xx}}{v^{2}}\right|+\left|\frac{\psi_{x}V_{x}\psi_{xx}}{v^{2}}\right|dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}\phi_{x}^{2}+\psi_{x}^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\psi_{x}\|^{2}_{L^{\infty}}\|\phi_{x}\|^{2}ds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\psi_{x}\|\|\psi_{xx}\|ds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{4}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{4}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.85)

Similarly,

μ​∫0t∫(UxV−Uxv)x​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s=μ​∫0t∫(Ux​xV−Ux​xv−Ux​VxV2+vx​Uxv2)​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s=μ​∫0t∫(ϕ​Ux​xv​V−Ux​Vx​ϕ⁡(ϕ+2​V)v2​V2+ϕx​Uxv2)​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫(ϕ2​(Ux​x2+Θx2​Ux2)+ϕ4​Ux2​Θx2+ϕx2​Ux2)​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0+C⁡(C0,M)​δ2​∫0t∫θ​ϕx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​dx​ds+C0,\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{U_{x}}{V}-\frac{U_{x}}{v}\right)_{x}\psi_{xx}dxds\\ \displaystyle=\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{U_{xx}}{V}-\frac{U_{xx}}{v}-\frac{U_{x}V_{x}}{V^{2}}+\frac{v_{x}U_{x}}{v^{2}}\right)\psi_{xx}dxds\\ \displaystyle=\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{\phi U_{xx}}{vV}-U_{x}V_{x}\frac{\phi(\phi+2V)}{v^{2}V^{2}}+\frac{\phi_{x}U_{x}}{v^{2}}\right)\psi_{xx}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int(\phi^{2}(U_{xx}^{2}+\Theta_{x}^{2}U_{x}^{2})+\phi^{4}U_{x}^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}+\phi_{x}^{2}U_{x}^{2})dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}+C(C_{0},M)\delta^{2}\int_{0}^{t}\int\theta\phi_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0},\end{array} (3.86)

and

|∫0t∫R~1​ψx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s|≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫R~12​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​δ2​∫0t∫(1+s)−3​e−c1​x21+s​𝑑x​𝑑s≤μ8​∫0t∫ψx​x2v​dx​ds+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\left|\int_{0}^{t}\int\widetilde{R}_{1}\psi_{xx}dxds\right|\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\widetilde{R}_{1}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\delta^{2}\int_{0}^{t}\int(1+s)^{-3}e^{-\frac{c_{1}x^{2}}{1+s}}dxds\\ \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mu}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\psi_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.87)

Substituting (3.84)-(3.87) into (3.83) shows

sup0≤t≤T∫ψx2​𝑑x+∫0T∫ψx​x2​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0+C0​maxx,t​θ.\displaystyle\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\int\psi_{x}^{2}dx+\int_{0}^{T}\int\psi_{xx}^{2}dxdt\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta. (3.88)

Multiplying (3.1)3\eqref{perturb}_{3} by −ζx​x-\zeta_{xx}, then integrating the resulted equation over ℝ×(0,t)\mathbb{R}\times(0,t), we have

cν2​∫ζx2​𝑑x+κ​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s=cν2​∫ζ0​x2​𝑑x+∫0t∫(p​ux−p+​Ux)​ζx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s−κ∫0t∫ζx(1v)xζx​xdxds−κ∫0t∫(Θxv−ΘxV)xζx​xdxds−μ∫0t∫(ux2v−Ux2V)ζx​xdxds+∫0t∫R~2ζx​xdxds.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\frac{c_{\nu}}{2}\int\zeta_{x}^{2}dx+\kappa\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds=\frac{c_{\nu}}{2}\int\zeta_{0x}^{2}dx+\int_{0}^{t}\int(pu_{x}-p_{+}U_{x})\zeta_{xx}dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad-\kappa\int_{0}^{t}\int\zeta_{x}\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)_{x}\zeta_{xx}dxds-\kappa\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{\Theta_{x}}{v}-\frac{\Theta_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}\zeta_{xx}dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad-\mu\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{u_{x}^{2}}{v}-\frac{U_{x}^{2}}{V}\right)\zeta_{xx}dxds+\int_{0}^{t}\int\widetilde{R}_{2}\zeta_{xx}dxds.\end{array} (3.89)

We will estimate (3.89) one by one. First, we have

∫0t∫(p​ux−p+​Ux)​ζx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s=∫0t∫(R​θv​ψx+R​ζ−p+​ϕv​Ux)​ζx​x​𝑑x​𝑑s≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫(θ2​ψx2+(ϕ2+ζ2)​Ux2)​𝑑x​𝑑s≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​maxx,t​θ​∫0t∫θ​ψx2​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫(ϕ2+ζ2)​Ux2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​dx​ds+C0​maxx,t​θ+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\int(pu_{x}-p_{+}U_{x})\zeta_{xx}dxds=\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{R\theta}{v}\psi_{x}+\frac{R\zeta-p_{+}\phi}{v}U_{x}\right)\zeta_{xx}dxds\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int(\theta^{2}\psi_{x}^{2}+(\phi^{2}+\zeta^{2})U_{x}^{2})dxds\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta\int_{0}^{t}\int\theta\psi_{x}^{2}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int(\phi^{2}+\zeta^{2})U_{x}^{2}dxds\\ \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.90)

It follows from Cauchy’s inequality, (3.45) and (3.82) that

−κ∫0t∫ζx(1v)xζx​xdxds≤C∫0t∫|ζx​ϕx​ζx​x|+|ζx​Vx​ζx​x|v2dxds≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ζx2​ϕx2+ζx2​Θx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​𝑑x​𝑑s+C0​sup0≤s≤t‖ϕx‖2​∫0t‖ζx‖|ζx​x|𝑑s+C0​∫0t∫ζx2​𝑑x​𝑑s≤κ8​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​dx​ds+C0​∫0t‖ζx‖​‖ζx​x‖​ds+C0≤κ4​∫0t∫ζx​x2v​dx​ds+C0.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle-\kappa\int_{0}^{t}\int\zeta_{x}\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)_{x}\zeta_{xx}dxds\leq C\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{|\zeta_{x}\phi_{x}\zeta_{xx}|+|\zeta_{x}V_{x}\zeta_{xx}|}{v^{2}}dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\zeta_{x}^{2}\phi_{x}^{2}+\zeta_{x}^{2}\Theta_{x}^{2}dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|\phi_{x}\|^{2}\int_{0}^{t}\|\zeta_{x}\|\|\zeta_{xx}\|ds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\int\zeta_{x}^{2}dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{8}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\zeta_{x}\|\|\zeta_{xx}\|ds+C_{0}\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle\quad\leq\frac{\kappa}{4}\int_{0}^{t}\int\frac{\zeta_{xx}^{2}}{v}dxds+C_{0}.\end{array} (3.91)

Similarly,

and

Substituting estimates (3.90)-(3.94) into (3.89) shows

sup0≤t≤T∫ζx2​𝑑x+∫0T∫ζx​x2​𝑑x​𝑑t≤C0+C0​maxx,t​θ2.\displaystyle\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\int\zeta_{x}^{2}dx+\int_{0}^{T}\int\zeta_{xx}^{2}dxdt\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta^{2}. (3.95)

By Sobolev’s inequality and (3.45), (3.95), we have

maxx,t⁡θ2≤2​maxx,t​ζ2+2​maxx,t​Θ2≤C0+C0​maxx,t​θ.\displaystyle\max_{x,t}\theta^{2}\leq 2\max_{x,t}\zeta^{2}+2\max_{x,t}\Theta^{2}\leq C_{0}+C_{0}\max_{x,t}\theta. (3.97)

maxx,t⁡θ≤C0,\max_{x,t}\theta\leq C_{0}, (3.98)

which, together with (3.82), (3.88) and (3.95), completes the proof of Lemma 3.6. □\Box

Finally, it follows from (3.45), (3.80) and equation (3.1)3\eqref{perturb}_{3} that

∫0+∞‖ζx‖2+|dd​t​‖ζx‖2|​𝑑t≤C0,\displaystyle\int_{0}^{+\infty}\|\zeta_{x}\|^{2}+\left|\frac{d}{dt}\|\zeta_{x}\|^{2}\right|dt\leq C_{0},

limt→∞‖ζ‖L∞2≤C​limt→∞‖ζ‖​‖ζx‖≤C0​limt→∞‖ζx‖=0.\displaystyle\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\|\zeta\|^{2}_{L^{\infty}}\leq C\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\|\zeta\|\|\zeta_{x}\|\leq C_{0}\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\|\zeta_{x}\|=0. (3.99)

Hence there exists some T0>0T_{0}>0 such that for all (x,t)∈ℝ×[T0,+∞)(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times[T_{0},+\infty), it holds that

−θ−2<ζ<θ+2.-\frac{\theta_{-}}{2}<\zeta<\frac{\theta_{+}}{2}.

θ=Θ+ζ>θ−−θ−2=θ−2,\displaystyle\theta=\Theta+\zeta>\theta_{-}-\frac{\theta_{-}}{2}=\frac{\theta_{-}}{2}, (3.100)

and

Finally, it follows from (1.1)3\eqref{ns}_{3} that,

θt+R​θcν​uxv−κcν​θx​xv+κcν​θx​vxv2≥0.\displaystyle\theta_{t}+\frac{R\theta}{c_{\nu}}\frac{u_{x}}{v}-\frac{\kappa}{c_{\nu}}\frac{\theta_{xx}}{v}+\frac{\kappa}{c_{\nu}}\frac{\theta_{x}v_{x}}{v^{2}}\geq 0. (3.102)

Define

We find

By the minimum principle of the parabolic equation, we obtain

infx,tθ¯≥infx,tθ¯|t=0=infx∈ℝθ0≥m0−1,\displaystyle\inf_{x,t}\bar{\theta}\geq\inf_{x,t}\bar{\theta}\Big|_{t=0}=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\theta_{0}\geq m^{-1}_{0}, (3.105)

which directly yields

infx,tθ⁡(x,t)≥m−10e−Rcν∫0t∥uxv∥L∞ds≥m0−1e−C0∫0t∥ψx∥L∞+∥Ux∥L∞ds≥m0−1e−C0∫0t∥ψx∥1/2∥ψx​x∥1/2e−C0∫0t∥Ux∥L∞ds≥m0−1e−C0∫0t∥ψx​x∥1/2e−C0​δ​t≥m0−1​e−C0​(t3/4+δ​t)≥C0​e−C0​t.\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\inf_{x,t}\theta(x,t)&\displaystyle\geq m^{-1}_{0}e^{-\frac{R}{c_{\nu}}\int_{0}^{t}\|\frac{u_{x}}{v}\|_{L^{\infty}}ds}\\ &\displaystyle\geq m_{0}^{-1}e^{-C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\psi_{x}\|_{L^{\infty}}+\|U_{x}\|_{L^{\infty}}ds}\\ &\displaystyle\geq m_{0}^{-1}e^{-C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\psi_{x}\|^{1/2}\|\psi_{xx}\|^{1/2}}e^{-C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|U_{x}\|_{L^{\infty}}ds}\\ &\displaystyle\geq m_{0}^{-1}e^{-C_{0}\int_{0}^{t}\|\psi_{xx}\|^{1/2}}e^{-C_{0}\delta t}\\ &\displaystyle\geq m_{0}^{-1}e^{-C_{0}(t^{3/4}+\delta t)}\geq C_{0}e^{-C_{0}t}.\end{array} (3.106)

Thus from (3.100), we have θ>min⁡{θ−2,C0​e−C0​T0}\theta>\min\{\frac{\theta_{-}}{2},C_{0}e^{-C_{0}T_{0}}\} for all (x,t)∈ℝ×(0,+∞)(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}\times(0,+\infty). By Lemma 3.1, 3.4-3.6, Proposition 3.1 is completed. □\Box

It is sufficient to show the same a priori estimate as Proposition 3.1. {ϕt−ψx=0,ψt+(p−P)x=μ​(uxv−UxV)x+F,cν​ζt+p​ux−P​Ux=κ​(θxv−ΘxV)x+μ⁡(ux2v−Ux2V)+G,(ϕ,ψ,ζ)​(±∞,t)=0,(ϕ,ψ,ζ)(x,0)=(ϕ0,ψ0,ζ0)(x),x∈ℝ,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\phi_{t}-\psi_{x}=0,\\ \displaystyle\psi_{t}+\left(p-P\right)_{x}=\mu\left(\frac{u_{x}}{v}-\frac{U_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}+F,\\ \displaystyle c_{\nu}\zeta_{t}+pu_{x}-PU_{x}=\kappa\left(\frac{\theta_{x}}{v}-\frac{\Theta_{x}}{V}\right)_{x}+\mu\left(\frac{u_{x}^{2}}{v}-\frac{U^{2}_{x}}{V}\right)+G,\\ \displaystyle(\phi,\psi,\zeta)(\pm\infty,t)=0,\\ \displaystyle(\phi,\psi,\zeta)(x,0)=(\phi_{0},\psi_{0},\zeta_{0})(x),\quad x\in\mathbb{R},\end{array}\right. where

and

G=(pm−P)​Uxc​d+(P−−P)​(U−r)x+(P+−P)​(U+r)x+μ​Ux2V+κ​(ΘxV−Θxc​dVc​d)x.\begin{array}[]{ll}G=(p^{m}-P)U^{cd}_{x}+(P_{-}-P)(U_{-}^{r})_{x}+(P_{+}-P)(U_{+}^{r})_{x}\\ \displaystyle\quad\quad+\mu\frac{U_{x}^{2}}{V}+\kappa\left(\frac{\Theta_{x}}{V}-\frac{\Theta_{x}^{cd}}{V^{cd}}\right)_{x}.\end{array}

Similar to Lemma 3.1, the following key estimate holds.

Lemma 4.1

For (ϕ,ψ,ζ)∈X⁡([0,T])(\phi,\psi,\zeta)\in X([0,T]), we assume (1.20) holds, then there exist some positive constants C0C_{0} and δ0\delta_{0} such that if δ<δ0\delta<\delta_{0}, it follows that for t∈[0,T]t\in[0,T],

‖(ψ,Φ⁡(vV),Φ⁡(θΘ))​(t)‖2+∫0t∫(ψx2θ​v+ζx2θ2​v)​𝑑x​𝑑s+∫0t∫P(Φ(θ​VΘ​v)+γΦ(vV))((U−r)x+(U+r)x)dxds≤C0,\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle\Big\|\left(\psi,\sqrt{\Phi\left(\frac{v}{V}\right)},\sqrt{\Phi\left(\frac{\theta}{\Theta}\right)}\right)(t)\Big\|^{2}+\int_{0}^{t}\int\left(\frac{\psi_{x}^{2}}{\theta v}+\frac{\zeta_{x}^{2}}{\theta^{2}v}\right)dxds\\[8.53581pt] \displaystyle+\int_{0}^{t}\int P\left(\Phi\left(\frac{\theta V}{\Theta v}\right)+\gamma\Phi\left(\frac{v}{V}\right)\right)\big((U_{-}^{r})_{x}+(U_{+}^{r})_{x}\big)dxds\displaystyle\leq C_{0},\end{array} (4.2)

Noticing that

ζ​ζtθ=[Θ​Φ​(θΘ)]t+Θt​Φ​(Θθ),\displaystyle\frac{\zeta\zeta_{t}}{\theta}=\left[\Theta\Phi\left(\frac{\theta}{\Theta}\right)\right]_{t}+\Theta_{t}\Phi\left(\frac{\Theta}{\theta}\right), (4.6)
−R​Θt=(γ−1)​P−​(U−r)x+(γ−1)​P+​(U+r)x−pm​Uxc​d=(γ−1)​P​(U−r)x+(γ−1)​P​(U+r)x+(γ−1)​(P−−P)​(U−r)x+(γ−1)​(P+−P)​(U+r)x−pm​Uxc​d,\begin{array}[]{ll}-R\Theta_{t}&\displaystyle=(\gamma-1)P_{-}(U_{-}^{r})_{x}+(\gamma-1)P_{+}(U_{+}^{r})_{x}-p^{m}U_{x}^{cd}\\[5.69054pt] &\displaystyle=(\gamma-1)P(U_{-}^{r})_{x}+(\gamma-1)P(U_{+}^{r})_{x}+(\gamma-1)(P_{-}-P)(U_{-}^{r})_{x}\\[5.69054pt] &\displaystyle+(\gamma-1)(P_{+}-P)(U_{+}^{r})_{x}-p^{m}U_{x}^{cd},\end{array} (4.7)

and

and

Thus we can finish the proof of Lemma 4.1 in the similar way as in Lemma 3.1. We omit the details for brevity. □\Box

It is easy to check that the other estimates for single viscous contact wave still hold for the case in which the composite waves are the combination of viscous contact wave with rarefaction waves. Thus, we complete the proof of Proposition 3.1, and finally prove Theorem 1.2.
